findings.quote: The buyback program's monthly ceiling only doubled to $4bn against $5.5trn of bonds outstanding, and long-dated yields are being set by fiscal policy running loose into repeated energy shocks rather than by who is buying.
findings.why: These figures and the procyclical-fiscal/energy-shock argument are TS Lombard's ('Fight The Treasury?' gives the $4B doubled monthly cap; GlobalData TS Lombard gives $5.5trn of outstanding bonds), while Goldman's note only says long-end buybacks are insufficient against the macro drivers of higher yields, so the sentence reads as Goldman's case using another firm's numbers.
findings.fix: Attribute the $4bn cap, the $5.5trn stock and the fiscal-procyclicality argument to TS Lombard, and keep Goldman credited only with the 'buybacks cannot fix the macro drivers' point.

findings.quote: Goldman moved the stock to Buy at $230.
findings.why: The context records a price target raise to $230 from $208 on an existing Buy rating, not a rating change to Buy.
findings.fix: Say Goldman raised its CrowdStrike target to $230 and stayed at Buy.

findings.quote: A further 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods is set to land ahead of it, taking total duties to roughly 20%, and the one-year trade truce expires November 1 (JPMorgan).
findings.why: The 7.5% tariff and the roughly 20% total duty level come from the Bloomberg Markets Live piece on China stimulus; only the September AI talks, the Sept 24 Xi visit and the November 1 truce expiry are JPMorgan's.
findings.fix: Credit the 7.5% tariff and 20% total-duty figures to Bloomberg and leave the JPMorgan tag on the talks, visit and truce-expiry dates.

findings.quote: Month-end MSCI rebalancing after today's close.
findings.why: Goldman's note says only that month-end MSCI rebalancing is expected to support momentum and risk assets, and gives no date; the month does not end at today's Friday August 28 close.
findings.fix: Drop 'after today's close' or move the bullet to This Week as month-end rebalancing.
